blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At Rootstock block 9,053,512 via the issuer-published public-node.rsk.co, non-proxy DoCToken.owner() returned MoCExchange 0x6acb83bb0281fb847b43cf7dd5e2766bfdf49038 and a zero-value transfer from an unrelated address succeeded. The verified DoCToken source/ABI has no pause, blacklist, freeze, or transfer-hook restriction, but exposes owner-only burn(address,uint256) for an arbitrary holder: eth_call from MoCExchange succeeded while an unrelated caller reverted. Money On Chain documents that this burn power belongs to the MoC system. The current verified MoCExchange implementation uses it in redemption paths, but MoCExchange is an upgradeable proxy in the documented governance route, so that system-owned path can be changed to seize or block holder value even though an active account blacklist was not observed. On Arbitrum at block 483,998,452, DOC 0x2ad62eb9744c720364f6ac856360a43e8a2229b5 is a verified non-proxy LayerZero MyOFT: owner() returned 0xb2395eaaeb03fb1f46647c423378b24f2e906305, local zero-value transfer succeeded, and the verified ABI has peer/delegate configuration but no holder blacklist, pause, freeze, or seize function. Those owner controls affect cross-chain reachability rather than a current local-transfer freeze. The issuer dapp is the public on-chain transparency surface; the reviewed official legal/sitemap and documentation set did not yield a separate terms or proof-of-reserves report, and the archived issuer route notice was retained for route continuity. Possible is therefore preserved rather than treating an upgradeable system-owned burn capability as direct false.

oracleRisk.summary: Money On Chain's pooled rBTC system consumes the OMoC BTC/USD feed, where up to ten staked operators use off-chain quorum signatures and elected fallback publishers. An April 2026 consensus-bypass flaw prompted a protocol panic pause; the protocol's incident report states the bug was fixed.

branchApplicability.rationale: Money On Chain documents one shared C0 bucket whose global rBTC coverage determines protocol states. DOC holders mint and redeem against the pooled system rather than opening borrower-specific debt positions, and the terminal liquidation state is a global, irreversible settlement that permits DOC redemption at the last available price. There are therefore no collateral-market liquidation branches to inventory.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: DOC is natively a Rootstock rBTC-collateralized CDP stablecoin; its Arbitrum deployment (0x2ad62eb9...) is a self-deployed LayerZero V2 OFT representation (contract name "MyOFT", canonical LZ endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c, ~37K DOC max supply). Money On Chain's own announcement (moneyonchain.com/doc-arbitrum) states DOC moves between Rootstock and Arbitrum via Stargate/LayerZero — a generic-OFT lock/mint route with a third-party (LayerZero) control surface, not the Arbitrum canonical bridge and not a Stargate canonical Hydra pool asset. This refutes the L2BEAT "Arbitrum Canonical" seed.
